The pie-chart given below given information about the number of students from five sections A, B, C, D, and E, of class 12 of a school to have appeared and to have passed in the final examination. 

The pie-chart on the left given the central angles of the sectors represent the students appearing in the exam from the five different sections, while the pie-chart on the right gives the section-wise numbers of students to pass the exam as percentage of the total number of students who passed the exam from all the five sections taken together. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e0e468e8b8a1368537242917724acd38d702296fdf70559a1dfb3888bcd0a3e0.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a13650c3b46632eb0a454312cc616b6e3afeb3002af383047c04df4156b42f0.png] 

Find the ratio of the average of the number of students who appeared in the exam from section A, B and C to the average of the number of students who passed from Section B, C and D.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e0e468e8b8a1368537242917724acd38d702296fdf70559a1dfb3888bcd0a3e0.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a13650c3b46632eb0a454312cc616b6e3afeb3002af383047c04df4156b42f0.png] 

**Concept Used:**

Basic Percentage Calculation

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total number of appeared students = 1800

⇒ Number of students who appeared from section A = (42)/(360)times 1800=210 students

⇒ Number of students who appeared from section B = (50)/(360)times 1800=250 students

⇒ Number of students who appeared from section C = (100)/(360)times 1800=500 students

⇒ Total number of students appeared from section A, B and C = 210+250+500=960

​⇒ Average number of students appeared from section A, B and C = 960/3

⇒ Total number of passed students = 800

⇒ Number of students passed from section B = (30)/(100)times 800=240 students

⇒ Number of students passed from section C = (25)/(100)times 800=200 students

⇒ Number of students passed from section D = (15)/(100)times 800=120 students

⇒ Total number of students passed from section B, C and D = 240+200+120=560

⇒ Average number of students passed from section B, C and D = 560/3

⇒ Ratio of total appeared to the passed students = (960)/(560)=12:7

**Hence, the ratio of total number of students appeared from section A, B and C to the number of students passed from B, C and D is 12 : 7.**

questions.question:
The given pie - diagram shows the expenditure incurred on the preparation of a book by a publisher, under various heads. Study the pie - diagram and answer the question that follows.

Various Expenditure (in percentage) incurred in publishing a book

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f37da0adc94580c7d84340a74936d32a28a8b2e9bd79e70fcb464463dba357b5.png] 

The marked price of a book is 20% more than the CP. If the marked price of the book is 30, then what is the cost of paper used in a single copy of the book?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹30

MP is 20% more than Cost Price (CP)

Percentage of expenditure on paper = 20%

**Formula used:**

MP = CP + 20% of CP

Cost of paper = 20% of CP

**Calculation:**

30 = CP + 0.2 × CP

⇒ 30 = 1.2 × CP

⇒ CP = 30 / 1.2

⇒ CP = 25

Cost of paper = 20% × 25

⇒ Cost of paper = 0.2 × 25

⇒ Cost of paper = 5

**∴ The cost of paper used in a single copy of the book is ₹5.**

If 2500 copies are published and the printing cost for them amounts to Rs. 160,000, then what should be the selling price of a book such that the publisher can earn a profit of 25%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of copies published = 2500

Printing cost of 2500 published copies = ₹ 160000

Printing expenditure = 20%

Profit percentage on selling a book = 25%

**Formula used:**

Profit = Selling price – Cost price

Profit percentage = (Profit/Cost price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Printing cost of a book = 160000/2500 = 64

⇒ Total expenditure on a book = 64 × (100/20) = 320

⇒ Selling price of a book = 320 × {(100 + 25)/100} = 400

**∴ The selling price of the book is ₹ 400.**
